title.narrative: Provision of life-saving nutrition support to the most vulnerable populations in underserved and hard-to-reach areas of Dinsoor District.

description.narrative: ltpgtBADEF is proposing a 12-month community-based nutrition prevention project targeting five underserved and hard-to-reach villages in Dinsoor District: Labawarod, Raaxole, Bilile, Kurman, and Waryaroy. These areas have been selected due to high levels of Global Acute Malnutrition, chronic food insecurity, displacement, and limited access to essential services for children under five and pregnant and lactating women. In line with the Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan and Nutrition Cluster priorities, the project aims to prevent malnutrition and promote early detection through locally led interventions that strengthen Infant and Young Child Feeding practices, improve dietary diversity, and expand access to lifesaving nutrition support.ltbrgtA key element of the intervention will be the deployment of 10 trained Community Health Workers, with two stationed per village. They will conduct routine MUAC screening, household visits, follow-up of defaulting cases, and timely referral of children and women to appropriate services. Over 1,200 caregivers will be trained on the Family MUAC approach to ensure early identification of malnutrition and promote prompt care-seeking. CHWs will provide door-to-door services for the delivery of vitamin A supplementation to 2,350 children aged 6 to 59 months and deworming to 2,115 children aged 12 to 59 months. Children and PLW identified with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) or Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) will be referred to a partner organization for treatment. SAM cases with medical complications will be referred to the stabilization center in Dinsoor.ltbrgtTo promote access to animal-source protein and improve dietary quality, the project will adopt a targeted Conditional Voucher Assistance model. A total of 1,900 vulnerable households will receive USD 40 vouchers redeemable from vetted vendors for a poultry package comprising a male and female chicken, 10 kilograms of poultry feed, and training on backyard poultry rearing. This intervention supports the One Egg Per Day campaign and is a key component of the project’s behavior change strategy. This will be designed to provide households with a sustainable source of protein to improve child nutrition. Voucher eligibility will be determined through a transparent, community-led selection process, ensuring accountability and fairness.ltbrgtBADEF will conduct 25 community-based cooking demonstrations to reinforce improved complementary feeding practices. Each of the five villages will host five sessions targeting both male and female caregivers. Demonstrations will focus on two key components: the preparation of enriched porridge using local cereals and legumes following the Tom Brown method, and practical use of eggs in children’s meals to support the First Foods strategy. These events will be facilitated by care group members, supported by CHWs, and conducted in Somali to ensure accessibility. The project will also form 50 care groups across the target villages: 40 for women and 10 for men. These groups will serve as platforms for peer-to-peer learning, behavior change communication, and ongoing counseling on IYCF, hygiene, and child health.ltbrgtTo promote equity and inclusive service delivery, BADEF will implement a deliberate minority inclusion strategy. This includes targeted mapping to identify marginalized groups in the five target villages and the development of tailored approaches to address their unique needs. Feedback mechanisms will be made accessible through various platforms and inclusive language, and data will be disaggregated by sex, age, and vulnerability to monitor reach and participation. The project will also actively recruit minority staff to reflect community diversity, promote cultural responsiveness, and enhance accountability to affected populations. This integrated approach will ensure that the most vulnerable are meaningfully included in all stages of the project.ltbrgtlt/pgt
